items.title: Chile's dark skies remain at risk despite energy project cancellation, scientists warn

featured_image.name: Light pollution is threatening the darkest skies on Earth. Here's how ...

items.description:
In one of the driest and darkest places on Earth, astronomers have secured a hard-fought victory to preserve the night sky — but they warn the fight is far from over.

AES Andes, a subsidiary of the U.S. energy company AES Corporation, formally withdrew its proposed INNA green energy project from Chile's Environmental Assessment Service in February, ending a yearlong confrontation between the scientific community and a sprawling industrial development planned just 10 kilometers from the European Southern Observatory's Paranal Observatory in the Atacama Desert.[1][2]

items.title: US orders global diplomatic push over alleged Chinese AI theft

featured_image.name: Where is DeepSeek AI Located? HQ, Global Offices & Company Insights

items.description:
The United States State Department has ordered a worldwide diplomatic campaign warning allies about what Washington describes as systematic efforts by Chinese firms to steal American artificial intelligence technology, according to a diplomatic cable first reported by Reuters on Friday.[1][2]

The cable, dated 25 April and sent to diplomatic and consular posts globally, instructs staff to raise with foreign counterparts "concerns over adversaries' extraction and distillation of US AI models". It names DeepSeek, alongside Chinese firms Moonshot AI and MiniMax, and states that a separate demarche has been sent to Beijing for direct engagement with Chinese officials.[3][4][5]

items.title: Study links record Antarctic winter heatwave to human-caused climate change

featured_image.name: 'Astonishing' Antarctica heat wave sends temperatures 50 degrees above  normal

items.description: During July and August 2024, parts of East Antarctica warmed by up to 28°C above average in the depths of winter darkness, making it the most intense winter heatwave in the 46-year satellite record. A new study published in Nature's npj Climate and Atmospheric Science in March 2026 has now attributed the event to a weakening polar vortex amplified by human-caused climate change — and warns such extremes could become up to 26 times more likely by the end of the century under high emissions scenarios.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. Navy intercepts sanctioned Iranian tanker in Arabian Sea

featured_image.name: CENTCOM confirms the interception of sanctioned tanker Sevan today.

items.description:
U.S. forces intercepted the M/V Sevan, a sanctioned vessel linked to Iran's shadow fleet, in the Arabian Sea on Saturday, as Washington continued to tighten enforcement of its naval blockade and global campaign against Iranian oil exports. A Navy helicopter launched from the guided-missile destroyer USS Pinckney carried out the interception, according to posts on social media platform X citing U.S. Central Command.[1][2]

The Sevan was among 19 shadow fleet vessels sanctioned just one day earlier by the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control, which described them as responsible for transporting "billions of dollars' worth of Iranian crude oil, liquified petroleum gas, and other petroleum and petrochemical products to foreign markets". The vessel was escorted back toward Iran under U.S. military watch.[3][4]

items.title: Macron calls EU defense clause 'stronger' than NATO's

featured_image.name: Leaders of France and Greece say the EU's defense splurge is no ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron declared Saturday that the European Union's mutual defense clause is "stronger" than NATO's Article 5, as he used a visit to Athens to reinforce Europe's push toward greater self-reliance amid deepening doubts over the United States' commitment to transatlantic security.

Speaking alongside Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis after talks at Maximos Mansion in Athens, Macron described the EU's Article 42.7 — which obliges all member states to aid any member that comes under armed attack — as "inviolable" and "not up for debate." He warned that "all our potential, or real, enemies need to be very clear about that."[1][2]

items.title: Chernobyl anniversary marked as IAEA warns damaged shield needs repair

featured_image.name: Chernobyl could face 'catastrophic' collapse as repairs stall following  Russian drone strike | Euronews

items.description:
As Ukraine marks the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on Sunday, the legacy of a Russian drone strike on the facility's protective shield continues to fuel fears of a new nuclear crisis in the heart of Europe.

On February 14, 2025, an Iranian-designed Shahed 136 drone struck the New Safe Confinement (NSC), the $2.1 billion steel arch built to seal radioactive remnants of Reactor No. 4, tearing a six-meter-wide hole in the structure and igniting fires in its insulation layers. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the drone carried a "high-explosive warhead" and accused Russia of a deliberate attack. Russia denied the allegations, claiming Ukraine fabricated the incident to disrupt peace negotiations.[1][2][3]
